rag.description: Run a MongoDB database command from an automation, for the work the typed plugins do not cover: creating indexes, reading collection statistics, validating a collection, or any other administrative command. The command document binds as BSON and the whole response is stored for the flow to read.

qa.answer: It runs any MongoDB database command the connected login may run and stores the whole server response as minified relaxed Extended JSON.
qa.question: What does the InvokeMongoDbCommand plugin do?

qa.answer: CommandText, CommandFile, or Base64 carries the command document and Database selects the target database. Outputs are Database, Ok, and Result.
qa.question: What are the key parameters and outputs of InvokeMongoDbCommand?

qa.answer: It runs as an Action task step with the database icon and the ActionRuleModel, and covers the administrative work the typed MongoDB plugins do not model.
qa.question: How does InvokeMongoDbCommand fit into an automation workflow?

qa.answer: Prefer a typed plugin when one covers the operation, restrict the rights of the connected login rather than trusting the command text, name the Database explicitly, and keep long commands in a file.
qa.question: What are best practices for using InvokeMongoDbCommand?

qa.answer: Use $type “Action” with pluginName “InvokeMongoDbCommand” and pass inputs in the argument, such as {{$ --Credentials:mongo-production --Database:shop --CommandText:{"collStats":"orders"}}}.
qa.question: How is an InvokeMongoDbCommand rule configured?

qa.answer: A malformed or empty command document, an unresolved database, or a server rejection fails the step; a command that answered without success stores Ok as false.
qa.question: How does InvokeMongoDbCommand handle errors?

qa.answer: It runs whatever the connected login is authorized for, including a drop, exactly like the script plugin of the SQL Server suite, so the login should carry only the rights the flow needs.

qa.question: What is the summary of InvokeMongoDbCommand?

Are macros resolved inside a Base64-encoded CommandText?
qa.answer: Yes. With the Base64 switch set, the action decodes CommandText and then resolves its macros, because the engine cannot see macros while the value is encoded. CommandFile content keeps its macros as written.

description: ### Purpose
Runs a raw MongoDB database command, which is the escape hatch of the suite.
Covers the administrative and diagnostic work the typed plugins do not model, such as creating an index, reading collection statistics, or validating a collection.
Stores the whole server response, so a flow reads exactly what the server returned.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature                    | Description                                                                                                                                      |
| Any database command       | Runs the command the first field of the command document names, such as `createIndexes` or `collStats`.                                          |
| Command as data            | Reads the command from CommandText, CommandFile, or Base64-encoded text and binds it as BSON.                                                    |
| Database selection         | Runs on the Database argument, then on the database the connection resolved, so the command never guesses its target.                             |
| Whole response             | Stores the complete response document, not a selected field, so nothing the server reports is lost.                                               |
| Branchable result          | Reports the `ok` flag separately, so a flow can branch without parsing the response.                                                             |
| Session and entity outputs | Stores outputs as Base64 session parameters named `InvokeMongoDbCommand:<Name>` and returns them in the response entity unless `NoEntity` is set.  |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case            | Description                                                                             |
| Index provisioning  | Create the indexes a later extraction needs, before the data arrives.                   |
| Capacity reporting  | Read collection statistics and report the stored size of a warehouse.                   |
| Maintenance         | Run a validation or a compaction command on a maintenance schedule.                     |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case             | Description                                                                        |
| Environment setup    | Create the collections and indexes a suite expects before it runs.                 |
| Server capability    | Read the server parameters a test depends on and skip the test when they differ.   |
| Teardown             | Drop a test collection in one call after the suite finished.                       |
### Notes
The command runs with the rights of the connected login, so it can also drop data; restrict the login instead of the command.
A command document with no field fails the step, because nothing names the command to run.
A server that rejects the command fails the step, so `Ok` reports `false` only for a command that answered without success.
Outputs are plain text in the response entity and Base64-encoded in the session parameters.
Stores the name of the database the command ran on.
Confirms whether the Database argument or the resolved connection selected the target.
Returned as plain text in the response entity for direct data transfer.

edge_cases: Index already exists with different options
Login lacks the right to create an index
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the server response in `InvokeMongoDbCommand:Result` and `true` in `InvokeMongoDbCommand:Ok`.
annotations.notes: Creating an index again with the same options succeeds and reports that nothing changed. The command runs with the rights of the connected login.

description: ### Create an index
The argument passes a `createIndexes` command that indexes the status field.
The step stores the whole response, which reports how many indexes the collection now has.

edge_cases: Database argument omitted and none resolved
Response larger than the session parameter a later step expects
annotations.expected_result: The step stores the statistics document in `InvokeMongoDbCommand:Result`.
annotations.notes: Database selects the target explicitly, which matters when the connection resolved another database. A step with no resolvable database fails instead of guessing.

description: ### Read collection statistics
The argument passes a `collStats` command and names the database explicitly.
The step stores the whole statistics document for a report to read.

edge_cases: CommandFile points to a missing file
File holds an array instead of an object
Command needs more time than CommandTimeout allows
annotations.expected_result: The step reads the command from the file, runs it, and stores the response in `InvokeMongoDbCommand:Result`.
annotations.notes: A long administrative command belongs in a file, which also keeps it reviewable. The Base64 switch never applies to file content.

description: ### Run a command from a file
The argument reads the command document from a UTF-8 file and raises the time budget.
NoEntity keeps the response in session parameters only.

edge_cases: Collection does not exist, so the server reports that the namespace is not found
Connection URI omits the database and no Database argument names one
Login lacks the right to drop a collection
annotations.expected_result: The step drops shop.orders, stores the server response in `InvokeMongoDbCommand:Result`, and stores `true` in `InvokeMongoDbCommand:Ok`.
annotations.notes: ConnectionString applies only when Credentials is not set. The URI carries the database in its path, so no Database argument is needed. Dropping a collection removes its documents and its indexes and cannot be undone.

description: ### Drop a collection with a connection URI
The argument passes a complete MongoDB connection URI instead of a stored credentials record, which suits a local or containerized deployment.
The `drop` command removes the orders collection with its documents and indexes, so a teardown step can reset a test deployment.

edge_cases: CommandText is not valid Base64, which fails the step
Existing documents do not satisfy the validator
Decoded text names no command in its first field
annotations.expected_result: The step applies the validator to shop.orders and stores the server response in `InvokeMongoDbCommand:Result`.
annotations.notes: The command document travels Base64-encoded with the Base64 switch set, so no text inside its JSON schema can be read as another argument. The switch decodes only CommandText; CommandFile content is always read as plain text.

description: ### Set a validator with a Base64-encoded command
The `collMod` command nests a JSON schema, and the Base64 encoding keeps the whole document as one argument value.
The command is encoded as UTF-8 Base64 and the `Base64` switch marks it, which also keeps a command with a space followed by two dashes intact.

edge_cases: Base64 switch is absent, so the macro inside the encoded text stays hidden and is not resolved
Value is passed plain, so the engine resolves its macros before the plugin runs
The payload comes from CommandFile, so its macros are kept as written
annotations.expected_result: The server counts the orders created today and the command reply is stored.
annotations.notes: The engine resolves the macros of a rule before the plugin runs, when the Base64 value still hides them, so the plugin resolves the macros of the decoded payload itself. Encoding also keeps any space followed by -- inside the JSON from being read as the start of another argument.

description: ### Count today's orders with a Base64 command that holds a macro
The argument binds the `mongo-production` credentials, a Base64 CommandText, and the Base64 switch at runtime.
The decoded payload is `{"count":"orders","query":{"createdOn":{"$gte":"{{$New-Date --Format:yyyy-MM-dd}}"}}}`; the New-Date macro is resolved after decoding, so the server receives the current date.
Stores the name of the database the command ran on.
Confirms whether the Database argument or the resolved connection selected the target.
The session value is Base64-encoded, so decode it before comparing or displaying it.

description: Reads CommandText as UTF-8 Base64 and decodes it before use.
After decoding, the macros in the decoded value are resolved, because the engine resolves the macros of a rule before the plugin runs and cannot see them while the value is encoded.
Use it for a payload that contains ` --` or `}}`, which end an inline argument value.
Invalid Base64 fails the step, so an encoded payload never reaches the server as text.
parameters.name: Base64

description: Reads the payload from a UTF-8 file, such as `C:\flows\filter.json`.
Applies only when CommandText is not set, so an inline payload always takes priority.
The Base64 switch never applies here; file content is always read as plain text.
parameters.name: CommandFile

description: Supplies the command as a JSON object whose first field names the command, such as `{"collStats":"orders"}`.
Required, because a step without a command has nothing to run.
Both Extended JSON forms are accepted, so declared BSON types survive the parse.
parameters.name: CommandText

description: Sets the time budget, in seconds, for connecting, selecting a server, and running the operation.
The value 0 means no operation timeout, so the step waits until the server answers.
Raise it for a long aggregation and lower it for a health check that must fail fast.
parameters.name: CommandTimeout

description: Supplies a full MongoDB connection URI, such as `mongodb://localhost:27017/shop`.
Applies only when Credentials is not set, so a stored credentials reference always takes priority.
Every connection setting, such as the host, the login, the replica set, and the TLS mode, is written into the URI itself.
parameters.name: ConnectionString

description: Names a stored MongoDB credentials record by name or id, such as `mongo-production`, so secrets stay out of the rule.
The record carries the host, port, login, replica set, and TLS settings, so the step never repeats them.
A value that carries a URI scheme, such as `mongodb://`, is used as a raw connection URI instead, and any other value that matches no record fails the step.
parameters.name: Credentials

description: Names the database the step operates on, such as `shop`.
Selects the database next to the collection, and replaces the database the credentials record or the connection URI carries.
A collection named as `database.collection` overrides this parameter in turn.
parameters.name: Database

description: Omits the response entity, so the step reports its outputs only as session parameters.
Use it when a later step reads the outputs by name and no data transfer is needed.
parameters.name: NoEntity
